newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Hamas stops short of claiming Jerusalem attack.
newsitem.headline: Hamas stops short of claiming Jerusalem attack.

text.p: A leaflet issued on Friday by the Islamic militant movement Hamas praised suicide bombers who blew up an Israeli market but stopped short of claiming responsibility for the attack.

The leaflet, faxed to an international news agency, called the attack "a practical response to the hostile Zionist practices against our people and our nation which has witnessed a noticeable escalation since the terrorist Netanyahu came to office in the Zionist entity".
Benjamin Netanyahu became Israel's prime minister in June 1996 on a pledge to bring peace and security. The two suicide bombers killed 13 people at Jerusalem's Mahane Yehuda market on Wednesday.
A leaflet issued in the name of Hamas' military wing on the day of the attack had claimed responsibility and given Israel until 9 p.m. (1800 GMT) on Sunday to free all Palestinian prisoners.
Israeli and Palestinian officials questioned its authenticity and the identities of the two bombers has yet to be established.

The new leaflet did not repeat the ultimatum. It said: "The Jerusalem martyrs attack was carried out by two heroes from the mujahideen (holy fighters) of our people." It did not say the two bombers belonged to Hamas.

Abdel Aziz Rantissi, a Hamas leader in Gaza who also suspected the authenticity of Wednesday's leaflet, said it was not yet clear who carried out the attack and whether Hamas was responsible for the Jerusalem market bombings.
"It is not clear yet. Everybody is waiting, however, experience taught never to confirm or deny a leaflet that is issued by the name of Hamas," Rantissi told Reuters.
Another Hamas leader in the West Bank said that during the past two years Hamas had adopted a new tactic.

"In the past two years, Hamas' new tactic was to carry out attacks and not claim responsibility or name the bombers as it did in the past to avoid the punishment of the families of the bombers, and for other reasons," said the Hamas leader who did not want to be identified.
"Maybe Hamas doesn't want to assist the Israelis determine the identity of the bombers. It could be waiting for the Israelis to solve the mystery," he said.

The new Hamas leaflet said: "The heroic Jerusalem martyrdom attack is a true expression of frustration among the Palestinian people...It is also the realistic option to resist occupation and liberating the land...Only the path of martyrdom will take us to our goal."
